title: Image of the next-degree cohomology comparison
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a category small in a universe containing the sites and coefficients [def-weil-size-convention], endowed with two site structures $\tau$ and $\tau'$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] such that every $\tau'$-covering is a $\tau$-covering. For $X\in\mathcal C$, let $\mathcal C_\tau/X$ and $\mathcal C_{\tau'}/X$ be the slice sites: their objects are arrows $U\to X$, their morphisms are commutative triangles, and their coverings are those whose underlying families cover $U$ in the respective topology. Let $\epsilon_X:\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C_\tau/X)\to\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C_{\tau'}/X)$ be the comparison geometric morphism [def-trf-geometric-morphism] with direct image the identity on underlying presheaves and inverse image $\tau$ sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. For $f:X\to Y$ write $f_{\tau'}$ for the relocalization morphism of slice topoi whose inverse image sends $H$ to $(U\to X)\mapsto H(U\to X\to Y)$. Higher direct images below mean the ordinary right derived functors on abelian sheaves, computed using injective resolutions. Suppose that a class $\mathcal P$ of morphisms and full subcategories $\mathcal A'_X\subset\mathrm{Ab}(\mathcal C_{\tau'}/X)$ have the following properties. Each $\mathcal A'_X$ contains zero and is closed under isomorphisms, kernels and cokernels of morphisms between its objects, and extensions (the weak Serre condition). Assume in addition:

(1) For $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathcal P$ and any $Y'\to Y$, the fibre product $X\times_Y Y'$ exists and $X\times_Y Y'\to Y'$ lies in $\mathcal P$.

(2) For every $f:X\to Y$, one has $f_{\tau'}^{-1}(\mathcal A'_Y)\subset\mathcal A'_X$.

(3) Every $H'\in\mathcal A'_X$ already satisfies the $\tau$ sheaf condition on $\mathcal C/X$.

(4) For $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathcal P$, $H'\in\mathcal A'_X$ and every $i\geq0$, one has $R^if_{\tau',*}H'\in\mathcal A'_Y$.

For each $X$, let $\mathcal A_X$ be the full subcategory of $\mathrm{Ab}(\mathcal C_\tau/X)$ consisting of sheaves isomorphic to $\epsilon_X^{-1}H'$ with $H'\in\mathcal A'_X$. For $r\geq0$, let $(V_r)$ mean that $R^i\epsilon_{X,*}H=0$ for all $X$, $H\in\mathcal A_X$ and $1\leq i\leq r$. Assume $(V_r)$. For $X\in\mathcal C$ and $H\in\mathcal A_X$, the canonical cohomology pullback
$$H^{r+1}_{\tau'}(X,\epsilon_{X,*}H)\longrightarrow H^{r+1}_\tau(X,H)$$
is injective. Its image consists exactly of the classes $\xi$ such that there exists a $\tau'$-covering $\{X_i\to X\}$ with $\xi|_{X_i}=0$ for every $i$. These comparison maps commute with restriction to objects of $\mathcal C/X$.

source.place: Tag 0EZC, lemma-V-implies-cohomology-extra-general; naturality/canonical maps are those of its proof and section-compare-general.

proof.text: Put $D=\mathcal C_\tau/X$, $E=\mathcal C_{\tau'}/X$, $e=\epsilon_X$, $G=e_*H$ and $m=r+1\geq1$. Since $e_*$ leaves the underlying presheaf unchanged, $G$ is already a $\tau$-sheaf. Its $\tau$-sheafification is therefore $H$: the identity map of this presheaf satisfies the universal property of sheafification. Thus the counit $e^{-1}G\to H$ is an isomorphism. All cohomology below is over the terminal object $X$ of the indicated slice site.

source.place: Tag 0EZC, lemma-V-implies-cohomology-extra-general, first sentence of proof; comparison morphism of section-compare.

proof.text: Apply [sk-thm-groth-ss] to $e:D\to E$ followed by global sections. Its site clause gives that $e_*$ preserves injectives and the first-quadrant sequence $E_2^{p,q}=H^p_E(X,R^qe_*H)\Rightarrow H^{p+q}_D(X,H)$. Use the Cartan--Eilenberg realization specified by [thm-sp-grothendieck]. By [thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences] its abutment has the finite filtration $H^n=F^0H^n\supseteq\cdots\supseteq F^{n+1}H^n=0$, with $F^pH^n/F^{p+1}H^n=E_\infty^{p,n-p}$. The abstract edge comparison lemmas used below apply to these categories: abelian sheaves on a small site are sheaves of modules over the constant integer ring sheaf, since every abelian group has its unique unital integer action; [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian] therefore makes both abelian sheaf categories Grothendieck. Global sections take values in abelian groups. The injective-preservation assertion above supplies the required acyclicity for this composite.

source.place: Tag 0732, lemma-Leray and proof, applied to e; finite filtration from derived.tex Tags 015N and 015J.

proof.text: The hypothesis gives $E_2^{p,q}=0$ for $1\leq q\leq m-1$, for every $p$. At $(m,0)$ every outgoing $d_s$ ($s\geq2$) has negative second coordinate. An incoming $d_s$ has source $(m-s,s-1)$, which is zero in the vanishing band when $s\leq m$, and has negative first coordinate when $s>m$. Consequently $E_2^{m,0}=E_\infty^{m,0}$. All intermediate graded pieces $E_\infty^{p,m-p}$ for $1\leq p<m$ are zero, so $F^1H^m=F^mH^m=E_2^{m,0}$. At $(0,m)$ there are no incoming differentials on any page; hence the stable term embeds into $E_2^{0,m}$. By the convergence convention [def-sp-convergence], the bottom edge identifies $E_2^{m,0}$ with $F^mH^m\subset H^m$ and the left edge factors as $H^m\twoheadrightarrow H^m/F^1H^m=E_\infty^{0,m}\hookrightarrow E_2^{0,m}$. We have proved $0\to H^m_E(X,G)\xrightarrow{a}H^m_D(X,H)\xrightarrow{b}(R^me_*H)(X)$ exact. This argument includes $m=1$, where the intermediate range is empty.

source.place: Tag 0EZC, lemma-V-implies-cohomology-extra-general, extraction of the displayed exact sequence from Leray; homology.tex convergence convention Tag 012U.

proof.text: Identify $a$ with the comparison map in the statement, rather than just some injection between the groups. Choose injective resolutions $H\to I^\bullet$ and $G\to J^\bullet$. The pullback construction [lem-weil-pbc-site-cohomology-pullback], using $e^{-1}G\cong H$, gives a map $\beta:e^{-1}J^\bullet\to I^\bullet$ extending this counit. Its adjoint is $\phi:J^\bullet\to e_*I^\bullet$, and in degree zero it extends the inclusion $G\to e_*I^0$ by the adjunction triangle identity. Apply [lem-sc-grothendieck-bottom-resolution-comparison] with $F=e_*$ and the second functor $\Gamma(X,-)$: it identifies $a$ with $H^m$ of $\phi(X):J^\bullet(X)\to I^\bullet(X)$. The same chain map computes cohomology pullback followed by the counit, because the pullback formula is the unit $J\to e_*e^{-1}J$ followed by $e_*\beta$, exactly $\phi$. Thus $a$ is precisely the canonical pullback of the item.

source.place: Tag 0EZC, first two sentences of proof; cohomology pullback via injective resolutions; derived.tex Tag 015N bottom edge.

proof.text: Let $P$ be the presheaf on $E$ given by $P(U\to X)=H^m_D(U,H)=H^m(I^\bullet(U))$. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-higher-direct-image-sheafified-presheaf], its sheafification is $R^me_*H$, and its unit sends a section cocycle to its class in $\mathcal H^m(e_*I^\bullet)$. To identify this unit with $b$, apply [lem-pc-grothendieck-cocycle-comparison] to $F=e_*$ and $\Gamma(X,-)$. Here $\Gamma(X,-)$ preserves kernels, so the supplied cycle lift $\Gamma(X,Z^m(e_*I))\to Z^m(I(X))$ is the canonical identification: both groups are the sections killed by the same differential. Its defining inclusion equation is the identity. The cited comparison says that $b$ takes the class of $z\in Z^m(I(X))$ to the section defined by that cocycle in $\mathcal H^m(e_*I)(X)$. Every cohomology class has a cocycle representative. Therefore $b$ equals the component at $X$ of $P\to P^\#$.

source.place: Tag 072W, lemma-higher-direct-images and proof, together with Tag 0EZC last sentence; derived.tex Tags 015J and 015N left edge.

proof.text: For the sheafification unit $\eta:P\to P^\#$ on $E$, its sheafification $\eta^\#$ is an isomorphism: applying the universal property twice, both $P^\#$ and $(P^\#)^\#$ represent maps from $P$ to sheaves, and the induced map is $\eta^\#$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-iso-locally-bijective] makes $\eta$ locally injective. If $b(\xi)=\eta_X(\xi)=0=\eta_X(0)$, there is a $\tau'$-covering $\{X_i\to X\}$ with $\xi|_{X_i}=0$. Conversely, if such a covering kills $\xi$, naturality of $\eta$ kills the restrictions of $\eta_X(\xi)$. A section of the sheaf $P^\#$ vanishing on a covering is zero, by uniqueness in its sheaf equalizer condition. Hence $\ker b$ consists exactly of the $\tau'$-locally zero classes. The exact sequence of Step 3, with the map identified in Step 4, proves both injectivity and the asserted image.

source.place: Tag 0EZC, concluding sentence expanded using sites.tex Tags 00WK (lemma-sections-sheafification) and 00WM (lemma-mono-epi-sheafification).

proof.text: The comparison commutes with restriction. Keep the two resolutions and the sheaf complex map $\phi$ of Step 4 fixed. For every arrow $U\to X$, evaluate $\phi$ on that object; the square with the restriction maps $J^\bullet(X)\to J^\bullet(U)$ and $I^\bullet(X)\to I^\bullet(U)$ commutes degreewise because $\phi$ is a map of sheaf complexes. The same holds for every further arrow $V\to U$ in $\mathcal C/X$. By [lem-weil-pbc-object-cohomology-presheaf-resolution], these section homology maps are precisely cohomology restriction, naturally in all these arrows. By the formula in [lem-weil-pbc-site-cohomology-pullback], the horizontal maps $H^m(\phi(U))$ are the canonical comparison pullbacks on $U$. Taking homology of the commuting squares proves the requested compatibility, independently of the chosen resolutions.
